events.title: Standardised framework for classification and presentation of Schemes under the NPS
events.whatHappened: CIRCULAR PFRDA/2026/47/REG-PF/10 28.08.2026 To All NPS Stakeholders Subject: Standardised framework for classification and presentation of Schemes under the NPS In exercise of the powers conferred under the PFRD Act, 2013, the regulations made thereunder and other enabling provisions, the Authority hereby issues this Circular prescribing the framework governing the classification, presentation, operation and disclosure of investment schemes [1] under the NPS. This Circular seeks to establish a standardised framework for classification and presentation of investment schemes, facilitate informed investment decisions by subscribers, promote comparability of schemes offered by different Pension Funds and prescribe uniform requirements relating to scheme naming, subscriber journeys, disclosures and implementation. Classification Framework 1. Classification of Investment Schemes 1.1 All schemes under NPS shall be classified in accordance with the framework specified in this Circular.
events.whyItMatters: This matters to employers, pension funds, NPS subscribers because it may change prudential, conduct, disclosure, onboarding or customer-protection duties in financial services. Teams should check scope, commencement and transition provisions against the source document. Implementation owners should map the instrument against existing policies, products and controls.

events.title: Dept of Consumer Affairs notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026
events.whatHappened: Dept of Consumer Affairs notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 | Akashvani News Dept of Consumer Affairs notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 The Department of Consumer Affairs has notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026. The Rules provide for Indian Standard Time (IST) as the common time reference across the country for legal, administrative, commercial and other official purposes. The common time reference will support accurate time-stamping of banking and digital payment transactions, coordination of railways, airports and other transport systems, and also the coordination of emergency and other time-sensitive services. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the Rules will come into force one hundred eighty days from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
events.whyItMatters: This matters to banks, consumers because it may change licences, approvals, inspections, penalties or recurring compliance work for businesses. Teams should check scope, commencement and transition provisions against the source document. Implementation owners should map the instrument against existing policies, products and controls.
events.sourceDocumentTitle: Dept of Consumer Affairs notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026
